title: Spec Keywords & Self-QC Checklist
summary: A practical checklist of high-signal controls keywords and how to use them to catch missed requirements.

blocks.content: Specs are long and controls requirements are scattered. Scanning for a fixed set of high-signal keywords is a fast, repeatable way to catch requirements you might otherwise miss.
Keyword scanning is a safety net, not a replacement for reading — use it as a final pass before sign-off.
Watch for: Occupancy / Vacancy, Daylight / Photocell, Dimming (0-10V / DALI), Plug Load control, Scheduling / Time clock, BACnet / integration, Emergency / Egress, and Networked / addressable.
Each keyword that appears in the spec should map to at least one captured requirement in your review.
For every keyword hit with no matching requirement, re-read that section. If it's a real requirement, add it and classify its obligation (NEED / SHOULD / CONDITIONAL).
Plug load and emergency/egress requirements are frequently overlooked — give them extra attention.

questions.prompt: How should keyword scanning be used in a review?

choices.text: As a final safety-net pass, not a replacement for reading

questions.explanation: Keyword scanning is a repeatable safety net used as a final pass, complementing careful reading.

questions.prompt: Which are high-signal controls keywords to scan for? (Select all that apply)
questions.explanation: Occupancy/vacancy, plug load, and BACnet are all high-signal controls keywords; landscaping is not.

questions.prompt: You find 'Plug Load' in the spec but have no matching requirement. What do you do?

choices.text: Re-read that section; add and classify the requirement if it's real
Remove plug load from the checklist

questions.explanation: A keyword hit with no matching requirement is a prompt to re-read and, if real, capture and classify it.

questions.prompt: True or False: Emergency/egress and plug load requirements are commonly overlooked and deserve extra attention.
questions.explanation: These categories are frequently missed, so they warrant extra scrutiny during self-QC.
